# Offline campaign compiler and replay certificate, version 3.0

The project is a multi-file typed model toolkit. Complete its offline pipeline:
layout compilation, symbolic-test recovery, scoped input validation, canonical
corpus assembly, and stateful test preparation. Run `python3 project/campaign_cli.py`.
Its JSON certificate is the graded interface; implementation organization is free.
The supplied AST/type visitor/graph APIs are useful editable project components.
This profile consumes recorded symbolic objects. It does not synthesize models,
execute generated C, invoke a symbolic engine, contact servers, or infer bugs from
model-return values. State machines and predicate semantics below are explicit inputs.

## Framing and domain

stdin is one UTF-8 JSON object, at most 64 MiB including whitespace. Duplicate
object keys, nonfinite numbers, invalid UTF-8, malformed JSON, and trailing JSON
produce exactly `{"error":"INVALID_INPUT"}` and exit zero. Otherwise configurations
obey all schemas, references, types, acyclicity conditions, and coupled bounds in
this document. Out-of-domain configuration validation is not required. Recorded
KTEST payloads may be arbitrary, including malformed data, and are handled per run.
Output is exactly one JSON object and exit zero; diagnostics use stderr.

The root has `types`, `modules`, `calls`, `pipes`, `entries`, `machine`, `runs`.
All lists preserve their given order unless another order is specified. Identifiers
are ASCII `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`, at most 32 characters, and unique in their scope.
Names in separate scopes may coincide. JSON object ordering is immaterial.

`types` is a list of named definitions with `name`, `kind`, and these extra fields:

| kind | extra fields | value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| bool | none | Boolean |
| char | none | one Latin-1 character, including NUL |
| int | `bits`: 1..64 | unsigned integer in [0,2^bits) |
| string | `maxsize`: 0..512 | bounded Latin-1 C string |
| enum | `values`: distinct nonempty strings | one listed string |
| array | `element`: type name, `size`: 0..4096 | ordered fixed-length list |
| struct | `fields`: ordered `[field_name,type_name]` pairs | object with exactly these fields |
| alias | `target`: type name | transparent value/layout alias |
| void | none | no value, only permitted directly as a module result |

Forward references and shared subtypes are allowed; the type graph is acyclic.
Aliases are transparent to expressions and values but retain their declaration name.
Strings recover bytes before the first NUL, or all maxsize bytes if none is NUL;
all maxsize bytes still belong to the symbolic inventory. String(0) recovers `""`.
Enum strings and state/command names are nonempty printable ASCII, at most 64 chars.
Struct field names are unique. No aggregate contains void. Type nesting depth is
at most 64. A result array/struct is a by-value symbolic result in this profile.

A module has `name`, `params` (ordered `[parameter_name,type_name]` pairs),
`result` (`[result_name,type_name]`), and `requires` (a predicate or null meaning true).
Parameter/result names are distinct. An entry's result may be void. Filters have a
Boolean result, although their acceptance comes from their `requires` predicate.
`calls` contains `[caller,callee]` dependencies; duplicate pairs have no extra effect.
A pipe is `{"target":module,"filter":module,"bind":{filter_parameter:target_parameter,...}}`.
Every filter parameter is bound once to a compatible underlying target parameter type.
Pipes are local to their target. A filter's own pipes apply transitively using the
composed bindings. Their acceptance is its own predicate AND its bound filters'
acceptance. Reusing a filter with different bindings means different applications.
Call dependencies affect compilation, not execution of predicates on missing helper
arguments. All call and pipe dependency edges together form a DAG.
`entries` lists distinct module names, in required plan order.

## Predicate language

Predicates are typed expression arrays. Configurations are well typed. A variable
refers to a module input, or the nearest enclosing `all` binding. Results are not
predicate inputs. `const` values obey the given type's JSON value representation.
In particular, a string constant is a literal Latin-1 JSON string of length
0..maxsize, including any embedded NUL characters. No truncation or padding is
applied to constants, including strings nested inside aggregate constants.
For String(3), `"a\u0000b"` is a valid three-character constant, distinct from
`"a"`; a recovered symbolic byte sequence a,NUL,b has the value `"a"`.
String(0) permits only the empty constant. NUL truncation applies only when
recovering symbolic string objects, not to expression values or equality.

| form | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `["var",name]` | lexical variable |
| `["const",type_name,value]` | typed constant |
| `["field",value,field_name]` | struct field |
| `["index",array,index]` | fixed valid zero-based index |
| `["all",binding,array,predicate]` | every element satisfies predicate, binding that element |
| `["match",string,pattern]` | full byte-string regular-language membership |
| `["not",predicate]` | Boolean complement |
| `[op,left,right]` | binary operation |

Binary operations: `eq`, `ne` compare same-underlying-type values deeply; `lt`,
`le`, `gt`, `ge` compare unsigned integers; `add`, `sub` use modulo 2^bits of
that integer type; `and`, `or`, `implies` are Boolean with left-to-right short
circuiting. `all` over an empty array is true. Binding shadowing is lexical and
must not affect enclosing/sibling predicates. Array indexing is statically valid.

Patterns contain printable ASCII. Grammar: union of sequences with `|`, sequence
of zero or more atoms, and zero or more postfix `*` repetitions on an atom. Atoms
are a literal, `(union)`, or a nonempty character class `[items]`. An item is a
literal or ascending `low-high` range. Backslash escapes the next character both
inside and outside classes. Unescaped `()[]|*\` are grammar symbols outside
classes; `-`, `]`, `\` must be escaped when used literally inside a class.
Other characters, including `.`, are literal. Empty pattern, empty sequence,
empty union alternatives, and repetition of nullable expressions are supported.
No anchors, dot wildcard, `+`, `?`, negated classes, or numeric escapes exist.
Matching is over Latin-1 code points with ASCII ranges; all other byte values
fail ranges that exclude them. Precedence is repetition, sequence, then union.

## Compilation certificate and symbolic wire identity

For each entry produce one plan with exactly `entry`, `modules`, `types`, `slots`,
`flag`, `variables`. `modules` is the root plus all transitive call/pipe prerequisites,
ordered so prerequisites precede dependents; among currently eligible modules use
lexicographically smallest name. Unrelated modules/filters are absent.
`types` lists enum, struct, and alias declaration names reachable from these
modules' params/results: dependency-before-user postorder, each declaration once,
first encounters following module order, parameter order then result, struct field
order, and array/alias child order. Primitive/array/string definition names are
not C declaration names and do not appear in this list.

`slots` is an ordered list of `[object_name,path,byte_width]`. `path` begins with
an entry parameter/result name, followed by field names and zero-based indices.
It describes the entry's own symbolic harness, independent of helper signatures.
The exact numbering contract follows the toolkit's `MainBuilder` convention:
inputs in parameter order, then non-void result, start at x0; each visited bool,
char, int, enum, string buffer, array, or struct reserves one increasing xN.
A scalar has one object; a composite itself has no object, then its children in
order reserve IDs recursively. String(N) has N character objects after its buffer
ID, not one packed object. Alias reserves no ID and adds no path component.
Even zero-length composites reserve their own ID. Void reserves none.
Widths: bool/char 1; int the smallest of 1,2,4,8 bytes holding its bits; enum 4.
Scalar object order is harness order, independent of KTEST object ordering.
If the entry has at least one direct pipe, one final scalar Boolean object is
reserved for `bad_input`; `flag` is its xN name, and it is not in `slots`.
Otherwise `flag` is null. `variables` is the total reserved ID count, including
non-object composites and any flag. An unused helper/filter consumes no entry IDs.

Each run has `entry` (one of entries) and `ktest` (standard base64 string, without
whitespace). Decoded binary KTEST v3 layout: ASCII `KTEST`, big-endian uint32
version=3, uint32 argument_count, then that many blobs; uint32 symbolic_argv_count
and uint32 symbolic_argv_length; uint32 object_count; then object name blob/data
blob pairs. Every blob is a uint32 byte length followed by exactly that many bytes.
Arguments are opaque and ignored (at most 64 arguments, each at most 256 bytes).
Symbolic-argv bookkeeping values are ignored. No trailing byte is allowed.
An object name is canonical ASCII `x` plus a nonnegative decimal integer with no
leading zeros. Every expected slot/flag occurs exactly once with exactly its width;
unknown or duplicate objects, including composite IDs, invalidate the test.
Object order is arbitrary. Leaf values are little-endian unsigned integers:
bool and flag must be 0/1, chars 0..255, ints must have all padding bits zero,
and enum indices must be in range. Strings consume all character objects even
after a NUL. Missing objects cannot be repaired by skipping to a nearby xN.
Any base64/binary/inventory/leaf-range error makes just that run INVALID_TEST.

The flag attests to pipe acceptance only: it must equal NOT(all the entry's
bound filters accept, transitively). A mismatch is INVALID_TEST, even if another
predicate would reject that run. Once this attestation is consistent, a false
entry predicate or false bound filter makes the run FILTERED. Results from the
recorded model never establish whether an implementation has a bug.

## Stateful preparation and corpus identity

`machine` is null for stateless campaigns. Otherwise it has `states`, `initial`,
`state_param`, `message_param`, and `transitions`. Every entry has those input
parameters: state is an enum over these states and message is a string.
A transition has `from`, `to`, `command`, `cost` (integer 1..65535), and `when`
(predicate or null). `(from,command)` pairs are unique. Its predicate is evaluated
on the recovered entry inputs, including the desired state, not an intermediate
simulation state. These guards are well typed for every entry. Transitions may
form cycles. Records and their preambles start from initial independently.

A usable preparation is a path of enabled transitions from initial to the
recovered desired state. Minimize `(sum of costs, number of commands, command
sequence lexicographically)` exactly. These supplied costs model replay setup
bytes/work; this is not a hardware timing objective. If no usable path exists,
mark the record UNREACHABLE. Otherwise append the recovered message to its
preparation commands. Corpus `cost` includes preparation only. For stateless
campaigns commands=[] and cost=0. The initial state needs no preparation.

A corpus identity is `(entry, recovered input values)`, excluding model result,
raw bytes after a string NUL, transport arguments, object order, and preparation
metadata. Arrays/objects/booleans/integers retain their JSON type identity; empty
arrays and empty objects differ. Never merge different entries. Assign corpus
indices by first usable run order; keep every usable witness run index in order.

Output has exactly `plans`, `records`, `corpus`. Plans follow entries order;
records follow runs order. Each record is one of:

* `{"status":"INVALID_TEST"}`, `{"status":"FILTERED"}`, or `{"status":"UNREACHABLE"}`;
* `{"status":"READY","case":index,"model_result":value}` for a new corpus input;
* same fields with status DUPLICATE for a later usable witness (even if its
  model result differs). Void model_result is null.

A corpus entry has exactly `entry`, `inputs` (parameter-name object), `cost`,
`commands`, `witnesses`. Invalid/filtered/unreachable runs never allocate corpus
indices. Transport/leaf/flag errors take precedence over FILTERED; filtering
precedes reachability; reachability precedes deduplication.

## Scale, development, and execution

One campaign represents a collected model-testing job, with shared types and
many symbolic witnesses; expanding every shared dependency path or recompiling
for every witness is not part of the objective. Bounds: 8192 type definitions,
4096 modules, 32 entries, 16384 calls+pipes, 16 params/module, 16 fields/struct,
4096 enum values, 64 type depth, 64 expression depth, 128 characters/pattern.
Across all entry plans at most 32768 scalar slots and 65536 reserved IDs;
across all runs at most 2,097,152 expected objects and 4,194,304 total
reserved-ID visits (sum of the corresponding plan.variables). Across usable
runs, preparation commands plus final messages total at most 16,777,216 Latin-1
characters, counted before corpus deduplication. These coupled replay-batch
bounds also cover empty aggregates and long state preambles. Predicate source expansion is also bounded per campaign:
4,194,304 expression-node instances and 8,388,608 match-byte units. For these
input-size guarantees, each operator/leaf is one node, an all-body is counted
once per declared array element, and a match contributes pattern-length times
(1 + its string type's maxsize). Count all branches conservatively. Sum the
entry predicate and every composed filter application plus distinct transition
guard ASTs, for each run. Identical transition guard ASTs count once per entry
per run; other applications count separately. These guarantees bound replay
work even for constant/nested predicates; no counters are required in output. At most 2048 runs, 4096
states, 16384 transitions, and 4096 composed pipe applications/entry. Preparation
may require thousands of commands; there is no additional hop cutoff. Coupled
bounds and the 64 MiB input limit all apply. Exact uint64 values remain integers.

Submit the full `/workspace/project` tree, at most 8 MiB and 256 entries (files
plus directories). All regular auxiliary files/directories are allowed and
collected; symlinks, hard links, devices, sockets, and FIFOs are forbidden.
No extension/name whitelist or extra-file rejection applies. The evaluator
freezes this tree and invokes `python3 -I -B project/campaign_cli.py`. Only this
project is submitted. Do not depend on sibling docs/checker, absolute host paths,
network packages, installed editable packages, or verifier files. The CLI's
bootstrap adds its local src/; no pip installation is needed.

Ordinary nonroot development commands, with all dependencies already present:

```
python3 /workspace/project/campaign_cli.py < /workspace/examples/smoke.input.json
python3 /workspace/public_check.py /workspace/project
```

The public checker runs real bounded children through normal stdin/stdout pipes.
Text, .buffer, fd0/1, fileno, fdopen, and explicitly flushed output before
os._exit(0) work. Empty/non-JSON/wrong/nonzero outputs fail. It is a sanity runner,
not a security boundary; direct root execution is refused. Public fixtures cover
only elementary layout and corpus identity, not the whole domain or maximum scale.
The nonroot public supervisor requires the development overlay documented in
WORKER-PROFILE.md; it restores the scored signal/group denials in each child.
Cleanup of the child's group and adopted descendants precedes acceptance on
normal and abnormal exits. Each fixture retains its120s deadline, plus at most5s
for cleanup; an enclosing controller allows300s for the two-fixture command.

Whole-campaign wall budget is 120s, motivated by offline campaign ingestion and
state-preparation latency. Local limits are 2 GiB address space/process,
180/181s soft/hard CPU per process, 64 processes/threads per leased UID, 256 FDs,
64 MiB/file, initial stack soft 8 MiB/hard unlimited, core dumps zero; stdout
512 MiB, stderr 1 MiB. No task sets CPU affinity. Formal requests 2 CPUs, 2 GiB
memory, no GPU. Runtime CPython 3.11.14, C locale, BLAS/OMP/MKL threads 1.
Python -I ignores PYTHON* environment settings; ordinary pipe buffering applies.

Scored execution uses immutable runtime/project in a nonprivileged chroot;
only /workspace/tmp is writable, cleared per invocation (use TMPDIR). /proc and
host/private task paths are absent. The complete syscall restrictions are in
WORKER-PROFILE.md; sockets/network, namespace/privilege changes, and listed
IPC/process-access syscalls are denied. Ordinary subprocesses/threads are allowed
within limits. Sampled scratch above 1 GiB regular-file size/allocated bytes or
50000 entries aborts as infrastructure error, not a hard storage quota or score.
Formal Docker/layers, cgroups/storage quotas, and transport attestation remain
formal_pending_docker. Local results never manufacture a formal reward.

# Evaluation syscall profile

The local evaluation worker uses a nonprivileged leased UID and a chroot with
immutable CPython/runtime/project. It drops supplementary groups and Linux
capability bounding entries and sets no-new-privileges and non-dumpable status.
No task code sets CPU affinity. Numeric limits and writable paths are specified
in PROTOCOL.md. The worker accepts native Linux x86-64 syscalls only: other
architectures and x32 syscall numbers terminate the process.

The following syscalls return EPERM:

```
socket socketpair connect
shmget shmat shmctl
semget semop semctl semtimedop
msgget msgsnd msgrcv msgctl
kill tkill tgkill ptrace process_vm_readv process_vm_writev
unshare setns mount umount2 pivot_root chroot setsid setpgid
setuid setgid setreuid setregid setresuid setresgid setgroups
open_by_handle_at name_to_handle_at bpf keyctl add_key request_key
perf_event_open userfaultfd io_uring_setup io_uring_enter io_uring_register
pidfd_getfd
```

`clone3` returns ENOSYS. `clone` is rejected with EPERM when its flag argument
intersects `0x7e820000` (namespace creation flags). Other syscalls pass this
filter and remain subject to UID permissions, chroot, and resource limits.
There is no extra no-fork/no-thread filter for this task. Parent cleanup uses
the leased UID and PID handles. `/proc` is not mounted inside the worker.

and adds the local src directory, so no installation is necessary. Run it with
Python 3.11.14. All runtime dependencies are in the standard library.

Several existing subsystem assumptions also need repair for the full profile.

The authoritative behavior and output contract are in /workspace/PROTOCOL.md.
All project files may be edited or reorganized. The output certificate is the
interface; private verifier code is never an import dependency.

"""Campaign compiler, typed replay, filtering, and state preparation.

Pipeline: compile per-entry plans (scoped module closure, declaration order,
symbolic slot layout), strictly decode each recorded KTEST, recover typed
values, verify the bad_input attestation, filter on predicates, prepare
stateful replay preambles, and assemble the canonical corpus.
"""

from . import ast as eywa_ast
from . import composer
from . import oracles
from . import run as eywa_run
from . import state as eywa_state
from . import wire


class _Context(object):
    """Per-entry compiled plan data shared by every run of the entry."""

    __slots__ = ('params', 'result', 'entry_pred', 'apps', 'filter_cache',
                 'guards', 'transitions', 'flag_id', 'expected')


def _parse_filter_pred(types, modules, filter_cache, name):
    pred = filter_cache.get(name)
    if pred is None:
        mod = modules[name]
        tenv = {p[0]: p[1] for p in mod['params']}
        raw = mod['requires']
        pred = (eywa_ast.parse_expr(raw, tenv, types) if raw is not None else None)
        filter_cache[name] = pred
    return pred


def _apps_accept(apps, inputs, types, modules, filter_cache):
    """Transitive acceptance of a tree of filter applications."""
    # Iterative post-order evaluation keeps deep pipe chains safe.
    stack = [(node, False) for node in reversed(apps)]
    results = {}
    while stack:
        (node, visited) = stack.pop()
        (fname, fmap, children) = node
        if visited:
            ok = results[id(node)]
            for child in children:
                ok = ok and results[id(child)]
            results[id(node)] = ok
            continue
        if not children:
            pred = _parse_filter_pred(types, modules, filter_cache, fname)
            ok = True
            if pred is not None:
                env = {fp: inputs[tp] for (fp, tp) in fmap.items()}
                ok = bool(eywa_ast.evaluate(pred, env))
            results[id(node)] = ok
            continue
        stack.append((node, True))
        for child in reversed(children):
            stack.append((child, False))
    ok = True
    for node in apps:
        ok = ok and results[id(node)]
    return ok


def execute(campaign):
    """Compile one campaign into its replay certificate."""
    types = eywa_ast.TypeTable(
        eywa_ast.TypeDef.from_json(t) for t in campaign.get('types', []))
    modules = {}
    for m in campaign.get('modules', []):
        modules[m['name']] = m
    calls = [(c[0], c[1]) for c in campaign.get('calls', [])]
    pipes = list(campaign.get('pipes', []))
    entries = list(campaign.get('entries', []))
    machine = campaign.get('machine')
    runs = list(campaign.get('runs', []))

    pipes_by_target = {}
    for p in pipes:
        pipes_by_target.setdefault(p['target'], []).append(p)

    plans = []
    contexts = {}
    filter_cache = {}
    for entry in entries:
        mod = modules[entry]
        params = [(p[0], p[1]) for p in mod['params']]
        result = tuple(mod['result'])
        if types.defs[result[1]].kind == 'void':
            result = None
        modlist = composer.plan_modules(entry, calls, pipes, modules)
        order = oracles.type_order(types, [modules[n] for n in modlist])
        slots, base = oracles.layout(types, params, result)
        direct = pipes_by_target.get(entry, ())
        flag = 'x%d' % base if direct else None
        variables = base + (1 if direct else 0)
        plans.append({
            'entry': entry,
            'modules': modlist,
            'types': order,
            'slots': [['x%d' % sid, path, width] for (sid, path, width) in slots],
            'flag': flag,
            'variables': variables,
        })
        entry_tenv = {name: tname for (name, tname) in params}
        raw = mod['requires']
        entry_pred = (eywa_ast.parse_expr(raw, entry_tenv, types)
                      if raw is not None else None)
        apps = composer.build_applications(entry, pipes_by_target, params)
        guards = []
        transitions = []
        if machine is not None:
            for t in machine['transitions']:
                raw = t['when']
                gast = (eywa_ast.parse_expr(raw, entry_tenv, types)
                        if raw is not None else None)
                transitions.append((t['from'], t['to'], t['command'], t['cost']))
                guards.append(gast)
        expected = {sid: width for (sid, _, width) in slots}
        flag_id = None
        if flag is not None:
            flag_id = base
            expected[base] = 1
        ctx = _Context()
        ctx.params = params
        ctx.result = result
        ctx.entry_pred = entry_pred
        ctx.apps = apps
        ctx.filter_cache = filter_cache
        ctx.guards = guards
        ctx.transitions = transitions
        ctx.flag_id = flag_id
        ctx.expected = expected
        contexts[entry] = ctx

    records = []
    corpus = []
    index_by_key = {}
    outcome_cache = {}

    for run_index, r in enumerate(runs):
        ctx = contexts[r['entry']]
        try:
            data = wire.decode_payload(r['ktest'])
            objs = wire.decode_objects(data)
            expected = ctx.expected
            if set(objs) != set(expected):
                raise wire.WireError('inventory mismatch')
            values = {}
            for (oid, blob) in objs.items():
                if len(blob) != expected[oid]:
                    raise wire.WireError('object width mismatch')
                values[oid] = int.from_bytes(blob, 'little')
            inputs, model = oracles.recover(types, ctx.params, ctx.result, values)
            if ctx.flag_id is not None and values[ctx.flag_id] not in (0, 1):
                raise wire.WireError('flag out of range')
        except wire.WireError:
            records.append({'status': 'INVALID_TEST'})
            continue

        key = eywa_run.identity(types, r['entry'], ctx.params, inputs)
        outcome = outcome_cache.get((r['entry'], key))
        if outcome is None:
            accept = _apps_accept(ctx.apps, inputs, types, modules, ctx.filter_cache)
            filtered = not accept
            if not filtered and ctx.entry_pred is not None:
                filtered = not eywa_ast.evaluate(ctx.entry_pred, dict(inputs))
            prep = None
            if not filtered and machine is not None:
                desired = inputs[machine['state_param']]
                enabled = []
                for (i, (frm, to, cmd, cost)) in enumerate(ctx.transitions):
                    gast = ctx.guards[i]
                    if gast is None or eywa_ast.evaluate(gast, dict(inputs)):
                        enabled.append((frm, to, cmd, cost))
                prep = eywa_state.prepare(enabled, machine['initial'], desired)
            outcome = (accept, filtered, prep)
            outcome_cache[(r['entry'], key)] = outcome
        (accept, filtered, prep) = outcome

        if ctx.flag_id is not None:
            want = 0 if accept else 1
            if values[ctx.flag_id] != want:
                records.append({'status': 'INVALID_TEST'})
                continue
        if filtered:
            records.append({'status': 'FILTERED'})
            continue
        if machine is not None:
            if prep is None:
                records.append({'status': 'UNREACHABLE'})
                continue
            (cost, prep_commands) = prep
            commands = prep_commands + [inputs[machine['message_param']]]
        else:
            cost = 0
            commands = []
        case = index_by_key.get(key)
        if case is None:
            case = len(corpus)
            index_by_key[key] = case
            corpus.append({
                'entry': r['entry'],
                'inputs': inputs,
                'cost': cost,
                'commands': commands,
                'witnesses': [run_index],
            })
            records.append({'status': 'READY', 'case': case, 'model_result': model})
        else:
            corpus[case]['witnesses'].append(run_index)
            records.append({'status': 'DUPLICATE', 'case': case, 'model_result': model})

    return {'plans': plans, 'records': records, 'corpus': corpus}

"""KTEST v3 builder for tests."""
import base64

def blob(b):
    return len(b).to_bytes(4, 'big') + b

def ktest(objects, args=(), sym_argc=0, sym_len=0, version=3, magic=b'KTEST'):
    """objects: list of (name, bytes) or dict name->bytes (order preserved)."""
    if isinstance(objects, dict):
        objects = list(objects.items())
    out = magic + version.to_bytes(4, 'big') + len(args).to_bytes(4, 'big')
    for a in args:
        out += blob(a)
    out += sym_argc.to_bytes(4, 'big') + sym_len.to_bytes(4, 'big')
    out += len(objects).to_bytes(4, 'big')
    for name, data in objects:
        nb = name.encode('ascii') if isinstance(name, str) else name
        out += blob(nb) + blob(data)
    return out

def b64(data):
    return base64.b64encode(data).decode('ascii')

def le(value, width):
    return value.to_bytes(width, 'little')

    return json.loads(r.stdout)

    {"name": "N8", "kind": "int", "bits": 8},
    {"name": "Str3", "kind": "string", "maxsize": 3},
    {"name": "Str6", "kind": "string", "maxsize": 6},
    {"name": "B", "kind": "bool"},
    {"name": "Pair", "kind": "struct", "fields": [["lo", "N8"], ["hi", "N8"]]},
    {"name": "Arr3", "kind": "array", "element": "N8", "size": 3},
    {"name": "Box", "kind": "struct", "fields": [["arr", "Arr3"], ["p", "Pair"], ["flag", "B"]]},
]

def check(name, requires, objs, expect):
    # module: params s: Str6, b: Box; result r: B
    mod = {"name": "m", "params": [["s", "Str6"], ["b", "Box"]], "result": ["r", "B"],
           "requires": requires}
    campaign = {"types": types, "modules": [mod], "calls": [], "pipes": [],
                "entries": ["m"], "machine": None,
                "runs": [{"entry": "m", "ktest": b64(ktest(objs))}]}
    out = run_campaign(campaign)
    got = out['records'][0]['status']
    assert got == expect, (name, got, expect, out)

# layout: s buffer x0, chars x1..x6; b struct x7; arr x8, elems x9,x10,x11;
#         p x12, lo x13, hi x14; flag x15; r x16 -> variables 17
def objs(sv, arrv, lo, hi, flagv, rv):
    seq = [("x%d" % (1 + i), le(sv[i], 1)) for i in range(6)]
    seq += [("x%d" % (9 + i), le(arrv[i], 1)) for i in range(3)]
    seq += [("x13", le(lo, 1)), ("x14", le(hi, 1)), ("x15", le(flagv, 1)), ("x16", le(rv, 1))]
    return seq

def ms(s):
    return [ord(c) for c in s.ljust(6, '\x00')]

A = [3, 255, 7]

# 1. add modulo: 253 + 5 == 2 (mod 256)
check("add", ["eq", ["add", ["field", ["var", "b"], "p"], 0] if False else
              ["eq", ["add", ["index", ["field", ["var", "b"], "arr"], 1], ["const", "N8", 5]],
                     ["const", "N8", 2]],
      objs(ms("hi"), A, 1, 2, 0, 1), "READY")

              ["ge", ["var", "v"], ["const", "N8", 3]]],

# 4. shadowing: inner all binding shadows outer; outer usable after
check("shadow", ["and",

        ["eq", ["var", "v"], ["const", "N8", 3]]],   # v unbound here -> ill-typed? no: v is not a param...
      objs(ms("hi"), [3, 2, 3], 1, 2, 0, 1), "FILTERED")  # inner shadow still sees 2 -> false
# 5. match on recovered (NUL-truncated) string
check("match", ["match", ["var", "s"], "a(b|c)*"],
      objs(ms("a\x00bc"), A, 1, 2, 0, 1), "READY")   # recovers "a"
check("match-full", ["match", ["var", "s"], "abc"],

# 6. const string with embedded NUL is literal, not truncated
check("const-nul", ["eq", ["var", "s"], ["const", "Str6", "a\u0000bc"]],

check("const-nul2", ["eq", ["var", "s"], ["const", "Str6", "a"]],

check("struct-eq", ["eq", ["field", ["var", "b"], "p"],

check("bool-eq", ["eq", ["field", ["var", "b"], "flag"], ["const", "B", True]],

# 8. implies / or / not

                              ["const", "B", True]],

"""Randomized differential test of state preparation vs brute force."""
import itertools, random, sys
sys.path.insert(0, '/workspace/project/src')
from eywa.state import prepare

def brute(transitions, initial, target):
    """Enumerate simple paths: min (cost, hops, lex)."""
    if target == initial:
        return (0, [])
    adj = {}
    for (f, t, c, w) in transitions:
        adj.setdefault(f, []).append((t, c, w))
    best = None
    def dfs(state, seen, cmds, cost):
        nonlocal best
        if state == target:
            key = (cost, len(cmds), tuple(cmds))
            if best is None or key < best[0]:
                best = (key, list(cmds))
            return
        for (t, c, w) in adj.get(state, ()):
            if t in seen:
                continue
            # prune: cost bound
            dfs(t, seen | {t}, cmds + [c], cost + w)
    dfs(initial, {initial}, [], 0)
    return (best[1][0] if False else (best[0][0], best[1])) if best else None

random.seed(1234)
for trial in range(400):
    nstates = random.randint(1, 6)
    names = ["s%d" % i for i in range(nstates)]
    initial = names[0]
    ntrans = random.randint(0, 12)
    transitions = []
    used = set()
    for _ in range(ntrans):
        f = random.choice(names)
        t = random.choice(names)
        c = random.choice(["a", "b", "c", "d"])
        w = random.randint(1, 4)
        if (f, c) in used:
            continue
        used.add((f, c))
        transitions.append((f, t, c, w))
    for target in names:
        got = prepare(transitions, initial, target)
        want = brute(transitions, initial, target)
        if got != want:
            print("MISMATCH", transitions, initial, target, got, want)
            sys.exit(1)
print("T10 OK")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Self-contained smoke tests for the Eywa offline campaign toolkit.

Run: python3 tests/selftest.py   (from the project root or anywhere)
Uses only the standard library and the local campaign_cli.py.
"""
import base64
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
CLI = os.path.join(HERE, os.pardir, "campaign_cli.py")


def b64(data):
    return base64.b64encode(data).decode("ascii")


def blob(b):
    return len(b).to_bytes(4, "big") + b


def ktest(objects):
    out = b"KTEST" + (3).to_bytes(4, "big") + (0).to_bytes(4, "big")
    out += (0).to_bytes(4, "big") + (0).to_bytes(4, "big")
    out += len(objects).to_bytes(4, "big")
    for name, data in objects:
        out += blob(name.encode("ascii")) + blob(data)
    return out


def le(value, width):
    return value.to_bytes(width, "little")


def run(campaign):
    r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-I", "-B", CLI],
                       input=json.dumps(campaign).encode(), capture_output=True)
    assert r.returncode == 0, r.stderr
    return json.loads(r.stdout)


def main():
    types = [
        {"name": "Count", "kind": "int", "bits": 32},
        {"name": "Flag", "kind": "bool"},
        {"name": "State", "kind": "enum", "values": ["INITIAL", "A"]},
        {"name": "Msg", "kind": "string", "maxsize": 2},
    ]
    mod = {"name": "query", "params": [["count", "Count"], ["enabled", "Flag"]],
           "result": ["answer", "Flag"], "requires": None}
    campaign = {"types": types, "modules": [mod], "calls": [], "pipes": [],
                "entries": ["query"], "machine": None,
                "runs": [
                    {"entry": "query", "ktest": b64(ktest(
                        [("x0", le(7, 4)), ("x1", le(1, 1)), ("x2", le(0, 1))]))},
                    {"entry": "query", "ktest": b64(ktest(
                        [("x2", le(1, 1)), ("x1", le(1, 1)), ("x0", le(7, 4))]))},
                    {"entry": "query", "ktest": b64(ktest(
                        [("x0", le(7, 4))]))},
                ]}
    out = run(campaign)
    plan = out["plans"][0]
    assert plan["slots"] == [["x0", ["count"], 4], ["x1", ["enabled"], 1],
                             ["x2", ["answer"], 1]]
    assert plan["flag"] is None and plan["variables"] == 3
    assert [r["status"] for r in out["records"]] == ["READY", "DUPLICATE", "INVALID_TEST"]
    assert out["corpus"] == [{"entry": "query", "inputs": {"count": 7, "enabled": True},
                              "cost": 0, "commands": [], "witnesses": [0, 1]}]
    # framing errors
    for bad in (b"", b"{", b'{"a":1,"a":2}', b'{"a":NaN}', b"[1]"):
        r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-I", "-B", CLI], input=bad,
                           capture_output=True)
        assert json.loads(r.stdout) == {"error": "INVALID_INPUT"}, bad
    # stateful preparation
    smod = {"name": "s", "params": [["state", "State"], ["message", "Msg"]],
            "result": ["r", "Flag"], "requires": None}
    machine = {"states": ["INITIAL", "A"], "initial": "INITIAL",
               "state_param": "state", "message_param": "message",
               "transitions": [{"from": "INITIAL", "to": "A", "command": "go",
                                "cost": 3, "when": None}]}
    def ms(s):
        return [ord(c) for c in s.ljust(2, "\x00")]
    seq = [("x0", le(1, 4)), ("x2", le(ms("hi")[0], 1)), ("x3", le(ms("hi")[1], 1)),
           ("x4", le(0, 1))]
    camp2 = {"types": types, "modules": [smod], "calls": [], "pipes": [],
             "entries": ["s"], "machine": machine,
             "runs": [{"entry": "s", "ktest": b64(ktest(seq))}]}
    out2 = run(camp2)
    assert out2["records"] == [{"status": "READY", "case": 0, "model_result": False}]
    assert out2["corpus"][0]["commands"] == ["go", "hi"]
    assert out2["corpus"][0]["cost"] == 3
    print("selftest OK")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
EOF
